summary: The note argues that small businesses are the lifeblood of the local economy, driving job creation, local spending, innovation, community culture, sustainability, philanthropy, resilience and entrepreneurial inspiration. Each theme is illustrated with a local business and its owner, such as Main Street Cafe, Bloom Bookstore and Tech Haven. It closes by urging continued local support for these entrepreneurs.
one_line: Small businesses boost the local economy through jobs, local spending, innovation, culture, sustainability, philanthropy and resilience, illustrated by profiles of local entrepreneurs.
key_facts: A Small Business Administration study found that since September 2023, small businesses have created 1.5 million jobs annually, accounting for 64 percent of new job creation in the United States.
Main Street Cafe, opened by Jane and John Doe on October 12, 2023, has already employed 15 local staff.
A Civic Economics study from November 2023 found locally owned businesses recirculate a greater share of every dollar in the community than national counterparts.
Bloom Bookstore was launched by Sarah Thompson in December of last year and sources from local authors and suppliers.
Michael Rodriguez opened Tech Haven in January 2024, offering customized tech services and workshops for local residents.
Emily Clark opened Classic Cycles, a bespoke bicycle shop, in February 2024 and organizes community rides and environmental awareness campaigns.
Alex and Anita Singh started Green Wrappers in March 2024, supplying plant-based packaging materials to many local businesses.
In April 2024, Oliver Martinez, operator of the local grocery store The Pantry, started a food donation program working with local shelters.
In May 2024 the town faced an unforeseen economic downturn, and small businesses adapted quickly by adjusting services, offering specials and partnering with each other.
Bella's Boutique, owned by Isabella Morris, switched to online sales and began local door-to-door deliveries during difficult economic times.
Max Peterson started the woodworking shop Timber Tales in June 2024, which led to mentorship programs for aspiring woodworkers.
Locally owned businesses make more local purchases, which minimizes transportation needs and reduces their carbon footprint.
